text:
maria: Heads-up — Customer A reported a spike of 504s and 5xxs during a burst at 15:04 UTC. They say requests to /v1/generate started timing out after ~120s.
kevin: seeing the same in prod proxy traces. Gateway backlog jumped, pool of inference pods stayed low.
ops-bot: INCIDENT created #INC-2026-4827 (autoscale/scaleup-lag)
support: customer escalated via priority channel, they need a mitigation ASAP — SLA at risk.
maria: initial quick dump: queue length on proxy spiked to ~850, avg token latency normal, but upstream connections returning 502/timeout. Repro when we replay burst (10x baseline concurrent tenants).
kevin: pulled metrics: HPA (GPU pool) didn't scale until ~90s after spike, KEDA ScaledObject shows cooldown 240s and pollingInterval 30s. That looks off for burst workloads.
nina: can you paste scaledobject/annotations? I suspect minReplicaCount=0 and cooldown too long + readiness failing on model-init.
kevin: pasted below:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: so-inference-prod
  annotations:
    scaledobject.keda.sh/cooldown: "240"
spec:
  minReplicaCount: 0
  pollingInterval: 30
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: inference-deployment
  triggers: [http, queue]
```
maria: also noticed pods start but never become Ready because of model bootstrap timeout in readiness probe logs:
```
[model-init] loading weights... elapsed 95s -> readiness probe failed: /ready timeout
[proxy] upstream connection closed before response
```
support: customer reported auth errors intermittently during the spike — likely collateral due to gateway overload, not auth itself.
sam: short-term mitigation options:
- increase minReplicaCount to 2 (prewarm)
- lower KEDA cooldown to 60s and pollingInterval to 5s
- temporarily route Customer A to dedicated capacity (if contract allows)
- bump readiness/startup probe timeout to 180s for model init
maria: I'm +1 on minReplicaCount bump and probe timeout. We should avoid immediate code deploys on prod, do patched k8s apply.
kevin: prepping patch now. Quick command to apply:
```
kubectl patch scaledobject so-inference-prod -n prod --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":2,"pollingInterval":5,"cooldown":"60"}}'
kubectl set env deployment/inference-deployment MODEL_PREWARM=true -n prod
```
nina: also open question: why model init > 90s? We added a larger model last week; maybe cache artifact stage on cold-start. Need long-term: pre-pulled model layers in image or model cache volume.
ops-bot: note: rate-limiter warnings during spike — billing tokens were getting throttled, causing additional 429s early on; that increased retry pressure.
support: staged mitigation applied? we told customer we'll route them to dedicated if they hit more issues.
kevin: patch applied at 15:21 UTC. minReplicaCount=2, pollingInterval=5, cooldown=60.
maria: monitoring — pods are coming up, readiness still failing on one replica that pulls model (~110s) but second replica warmed in ~70s. Proxy queues dropping and 504s falling.
support: customer on call confirmed reduced errors, still saw a couple but much improved :thumbsup:
sam: follow-ups to capture in runbook:
- For tenant-burst scenarios, ensure minReplicaCount >=1 for customers above X qps
- KEDA pollingInterval should be <= polling window for expected burst
- Cooldown <= 60s for rapid recovery
- Add a startupProbe with extended timeout for model loads
- Provision a fallback smaller model variant to serve quick low-latency responses
nina: creating an issue for model prewarm infra: attach model cache PV to nodepool and pre-download during node boot.
kevin: logging patch diff and metrics snapshot in #eng-sre. Repro steps saved:
1) hammer proxy with 200 concurrent requests from single tenant for 60s
2) observe scaledobject metric -> KEDA poll -> scale up delay
3) check readiness logs for model init timeout
maria: owners: kevin -> apply k8s mitigations, nina -> prewarm infra ticket, sam -> update runbook & customer comms, support -> confirm SLA remediation with customer.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, status: recovery in progress, link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-4827
maria: will keep thread open for any regression. If we see repeated pattern, plan an emergency opt-in for Dedicated for high-burst tenants.
kevin: plan for next week: test scaledobject with synthetic bursts in staging for different model sizes and tune KEDA params.
maria: thanks all. Closing note: short-term fix worked, need infra changes to avoid repeating. :rotating_light:
